findings.title: English file path lookup fails for different theme bases (login/account/admin/email)
findings.body: englishFile is computed by regex-replacing the locale suffix in the current file's absolute path, assuming the English file lives in the exact same directory with the same basename structure. For files under resources-community vs resources, and across different theme categories (account/login/admin/email), this heuristic may not reliably resolve to the actual English source file if directory layouts differ, silently falling back to empty string on exception, masking real validation issues since englishValue becomes "" and HTML in translations would then be verified against the strict POLICY_NO_HTML even when the English source legitimately contains HTML.

findings.title: verify() swallows exceptions from verifySafeHtml as RuntimeException, not reported as validation messages
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() throws RuntimeException (not caught) when the matching English file cannot be opened (e.g., FileNotFoundException wrapped), causing the whole verify() call to crash with an unchecked exception instead of being reported as a validation message or at least a graceful failure. This could crash the build in unexpected ways for any properties file whose matching English file path can't be resolved (e.g., for files that don't have a direct English equivalent at the predictable path), rather than failing with a clear verifier message.

findings.title: santizeAnchors mutates matcher position asymmetrically causing potential false positives/negatives
findings.body: santizeAnchors matches anchor tags in value with Matcher.find() in a loop, but calls value.replaceFirst() inside the loop which does not update the matcher's underlying input, so subsequent find() calls continue to scan the original (unmodified) value string, not the updated one. If value contains multiple anchors, this can produce incorrect pairing between value's anchors and englishValue's anchors, leading to incorrect 'Didn't find anchor tag' messages or missed detections.

findings.title: normalizeValue special-casing by key name is fragile and incomplete
findings.body: The sanitizer special-cases specific keys like "templateHelp", "optimizeLookupHelp", and key prefixes like "linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit" or "error-invalid-multivalued-size" to strip out patterns resembling HTML tags (e.g. '<NAME>', '<Extensions>', MessageFormat choice patterns). This is a maintenance burden: any new translation key containing legitimate '<' usage (e.g. other MessageFormat choice patterns, generic placeholders) not in this hardcoded list will trigger false-positive 'Illegal HTML' errors, as seen already needing special handling for multiple distinct keys across different locale files in this PR.
